REPORT
Date May 18, 1939
Subject Allegations made by Peter E. Eustaff, alias Evstafieff against
A. A. Nogaitzeff.
Made by. D...ide Forwarded by. Wagan A.S.P.

Inquiries have elicited the following
information in connection with the attached letters
containing allegations against A.A. Nogaitzeff
written by Peter E. Eustaff, alias Evstafieff
to Mr. R. T. Leyton-Griffin, Editor of the
North China Daily News.

Eustaff, who is employed as a proof-reader
by the North China Daily News, states that he first
became acquainted with Nogaitzeff, who is connected
with the management of the Evening Echo, whilst
employed as a proof-reader by that paper during
November 1933.

Towards the end of April, 1939, Nogaitzeff
met Eustaff at the Navy Y.M.C.A. and made him a
proposition to the effect that he was empowered by
a certain party to offer $200.00 for information
regarding the authorship of a letter on the subject
of "Gestapo Arrests" which appeared in the North
China Daily News of March 22nd, 1939.

Nogaitzeff subsequently met Eustaff from
time to time but was non-committal regarding the
offer and when pressed for a definite answer on
May 16th, he alleged that there were prospects of
obtaining the requisite information from another
source, but that confirmation would probably be
required. He also informed Eustaff that the

事由：彼得·E·尤斯塔夫（Peter E. Eustaff），又名叶夫斯塔菲耶夫（Evstafieff），对 A. A. 诺盖采夫（A. A. Nogaitzeff）提出的指控。
呈报人：D...ide 转呈人：Wagan 助理副巡官

就随附的由彼得·E·尤斯塔夫（又名叶夫斯塔菲耶夫）写给《字林西报》编辑 R. T. 莱顿-格里芬（R. T. Leyton-Griffin）先生、包含针对 A.A. 诺盖采夫指控的信件而言，经查询获悉以下信息。

尤斯塔夫受雇于《字林西报》担任校对员，他称自己初次结识与《晚声报》（Evening Echo）管理层有关联的诺盖采夫，是在1933年11月期间，当时他在该报担任校对员。

1939年4月底，诺盖采夫在海军青年会（Navy Y.M.C.A.）会见尤斯塔夫，并向其提出一项提议，大意是他受某方授权，愿出价200.00美元，以获取关于1939年3月22日刊登在《字林西报》上题为“盖世太保逮捕行动”一信的作者身份的情报。

此后，诺盖采夫不时与尤斯塔夫会面，但对该提议未作明确承诺；当尤斯塔夫在5月16日追问确切答复时，诺盖采夫声称有望从另一来源获取所需情报，但可能需要进行核实。他还告知尤斯塔夫，他为之工作的那一方

Referring to Nogaitzeff's statement
that the information might be obtained from
an alternative source, Mr. Peyton-Griffin has
stated that the identity of the writer is kept
under lock and key and is known to no one but
himself.
Eustoff, alias Evstafieff previously
came to the notice of the Municipal Police
on April 24th, 1933 when he appeared before
the Shanghai Special District Court on a charge
of misappropriation and was sentenced to six
months imprisonment suspended for three years.
He again appeared before the Court on July
17th, 1934 and was sentenced to eight months
imprisonment on a charge of larceny and fraud
and ordered to serve his previous sentence.
Nogaitzeff is a Russian journalist who

China Daily News, the Evening Echo and other
newspapers. He was formerly secretary of the

                                        D.C. (Special Branch)

Shanghai, May 16, 1939.

L. W. Hide
(BOS) Headquarters.

Dear Sir,
As requested by you to give all particulars regarding
the bribe of two hundred dollars offered me by a man
named A.A. Nagaitzeff (name obtained from the Staff of the
Evening Echo) I wish to say that I first associated with
this man sometime in November last when I did some
proof-reading for the Evening Echo.
In December, however, of the same year, for private
reasons I could not continue working for them and so left
in spite of their offers to me for a higher pay to remain,
nevertheless A.A. Nagaitzeff, many a time on meeting me
at the Navy Y.M.C.A. restaurant, persisted in making me
change my opinion until one day he suddenly asked me
if I wanted to make two hundred dollars, this excited my
curiosity and interest and as I was interested he told
me to obtain somehow the name of the person who wrote a
letter to the editor of the North China Daily News, "The Bund
Shanghai" where I am employed, which subject I later
discovered to be on "Gestapo Arrests"
In the meantime, I agreed before him to do so
and on leaving him reported the matter to my present
editor to whom I already made a written statement
up to that time of writing.

上海，1939年5月16日。

L. W. 海德（Hide）
（BOS）总部。

尊敬的先生：
应您要求，我就一名叫 A.A. 纳盖采夫（A.A. Nagaitzeff）（姓名从《晚声报》职员处获知）的男子向我提供两百美元贿赂一事提供所有细节，我想说明的是，我去年11月左右首次与此人结识，当时我为《晚声报》做一些校对工作。
然而，同年12月，出于个人原因，我无法继续为他们工作，因此离职，尽管他们提出加薪挽留我，但 A.A. 纳盖采夫多次在海军青年会餐厅遇见我时，坚持要我改变主意，直到有一天他突然问我是否想赚两百美元，这激起了我的好奇心和兴趣，鉴于我表现出兴趣，他让我设法获取写给我所供职的《字林西报》（The Bund Shanghai）编辑的一封信的作者姓名，后来我发现该信主题是关于“盖世太保逮捕行动”
在此期间，我当面答应了他，离开后便向现任编辑汇报了此事，并在撰写此信之前已向编辑提交了书面陈述。

Ever since I called on the police as advised by my editor
there was some difficulty in trying to reach him to discuss
whether the other party (unknown to me) still wanted the
name until today when I met him and pressed him
again about the outcome of his conversation with that
certain other man or men. He told me not to talk
loud and he had mentioned to the other party that
the letter writer's name could be disclosed and
while on the subject he asked me to keep all my
contacts open with the North China Daily News and to
wait as he half-thought that the other party
had an idea of who the writer was but formed the
idea that a confirmation from me would be eventually
required - Anyway, he asked me to keep everything
open as that party would always be willing to
pay for any information wanted by them in future
and asked me to be very careful and to let
no one know about this! This is all till
the time of writing.

Sincerely yours
Peter A. Eustaff.
c/o North China Daily News
17 The Bund.
Shanghai.

自从我听从编辑建议拜访警方以来，在试图联系他以讨论另一方（我不知其身份）是否仍想要该姓名方面遇到了一些困难，直到今天我见到他并再次向他施压，询问他与那一位或那些人的谈话结果。他告诉我不要大声说话，并说他已向另一方提及可以披露信件作者的姓名，在此话题中，他要求我与《字林西报》保持所有联系渠道畅通并等待，因为他半认为另一方已经知道作者是谁，但认为最终需要从我这里得到确认——总之，他要求我对一切保持开放态度，因为该方将来总是愿意为他们想要的任何情报付费，并要求我非常小心，不让任何人知道此事！这就是截至写信时的全部情况。

您真诚的
彼得·A·尤斯塔夫（Peter A. Eustaff）。

外滩17号。

NAVY Y. M. C. A.
SHANGHAI
CHINA

Shanghai, May 29, 1939

Dear Mr Griffin.

As an employee of the North China Daily
News, I feel it my duty to inform you of a
bribe that was offered me to divulge the name
of a correspondent to Letters to the Editor in
the issue of March 22, 1939.

Some days ago, I met a man whom
I first saw at the Shanghai Evening Echo,
where I did some part-time proofreading.
We do not know each other otherwise
but he strikes me as being some kind
of a partner in the said firm.

This man approached me one night
at the YMCA where I live and was
prepared to hand me $200.-
(two hundred dollars in local currency)
the moment I crossed the original letter
over to him which is believed to be
written by a German.

It may be claimed that I agreed
to do so without any intention of doing so,
it is my hope to assist you if you are
interested in the matter to see the
real motive behind this bribe remain

Yours respectfully
Peter B. Eustaff.
Proofreader

上海，1939年5月29日

亲爱的格里芬先生：

作为《字林西报》的一名雇员，我觉得我有责任向您通报，有人向我行贿，企图让我泄露1939年3月22日一期“读者来信”栏目中一位通讯员的姓名。

几天前，我遇到一个人，我第一次见到他是在《上海晚声报》，我当时在那里做兼职校对。
除此之外我们互不相识，但他给我的印象是上述报社的某种合伙人。

这个人某天晚上在我居住的青年会接近我，
并准备在我将原始信件交给他那一刻
付给我200美元.-
（当地货币两百美元），据信该信
是由一名德国人写的。

或许可以说，我虽然表面上同意这样做，但内心并无此意，我希望如果您对此事感兴趣，能协助您看清这笔贿赂背后的真实动机，保持

您恭敬的
彼得·B·尤斯塔夫（Peter B. Eustaff）。
校对员

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

MAR 22 1939

Gestapo Arrests:
Another German's Views
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Allow me to give my opinion
on WOLF SCHENKE's letter re "Gestapo
Arrests."
I am German, not Jewish, and left
Germany about two years ago. I
don't want you to publish my name
; I like my relatives to live further
on in Germany.
I have been in Prague and met
there quite a number of these so
called "traitors," who seemed to me
much better Germans than those
governing Germany at the time being.
They had to leave Germany as that
was their only chance to serve their
country in the future. The only de-
lict to be claimed against these
political refugees is, that they served
their country before 1933. No other
country would even think of arresting
the members of a gone government
as is the custom of the Gestapo.
Besides, I am absolutely sure that
lots of Czechs are arrested by the
"Gestapo." Most of Czechoslovakias
inhabitants hated Germany with all
their heart, and will go on to hate
them until either all of them are
killed or until there will be no more
Gestapo in all Europe.
May I congratulate Mr. SCHENKE on
the coup of his Fuehrer, hoping that
Czechoslovakia will be ripe enough
to hang him.
GERMAN WITH HIS OWN IDEAS.
Shanghai, Mar. 21.

《字林西报》。

1939年3月22日

盖世太保逮捕行动：
另一位德国人的观点
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——请允许我就沃尔夫·申克（WOLF SCHENKE）关于“盖世太保逮捕行动”的信件发表我的看法。
我是德国人，不是犹太人，大约两年前离开德国。我不希望您公布我的姓名；我希望我的亲属能在德国继续生活下去。
我曾到过布拉格，在那里遇到了不少这些所谓的“叛徒”，在我看来，他们比当时统治德国的德国人要好得多。他们不得不离开德国，因为那是他们未来报效祖国的唯一机会。对这些政治难民唯一可指责的过失是，他们在1933年之前曾为国效力。没有任何其他国家会像盖世太保那样，甚至想到去逮捕一个已下台政府的成员。
此外，我绝对确信许多捷克人被“盖世太保”逮捕。大多数捷克斯洛伐克居民全心全意地憎恨德国，并将继续憎恨他们，直到要么他们全部被杀，要么整个欧洲不再有盖世太保。
我可以祝贺申克先生的元首取得了政变成功，希望捷克斯洛伐克足够成熟，能够将他绞死。
持有自己思想的德国人。
上海，3月21日。
